title: Route Roadbook Generator: Printable Leg Table
description: Turn a route into a printable roadbook with the Route Roadbook Generator — clean leg table, cumulative totals, ready for PDF. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a five-stop tour becomes five leg rows with distances, times and cumulative totals — the document a co-driver can navigate from while the driver watches the road.
quick_answer: The Route Roadbook Generator takes a route built from your start, stops and destination and lays it out as a clean roadbook: a leg-by-leg table with distances, times and cumulative totals, ready to print or save as a PDF. Build the route, generate the book, and carry it on paper.

faq: Does it include turn-by-turn instructions?
The roadbook is a leg table — distances, times and totals per hop — not a turn list. It navigates by legs, the way rally books do; junction-level guidance is a navigation app's craft.
How do I save it?
Print it, or save the print view as a PDF — both are the intended outputs, designed for paper from the start.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Leg times are routing estimates; the printed book is a plan, and plans get margins, not traffic feeds.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Legs are road distances — the book's whole honesty is that its numbers are the driven ones.
Can route results change over time?
Regenerate per trip: road data improves, and a roadbook's authority expires with the route it describes.
How many legs can it hold?
As many as the route builders hold — the multi-stop family routes up to 30 stops, and each becomes a row.
Is it only for cars?
Legs are legs: the trek version day-splits walks, and cyclists read roadbooks happily. The table serves any routed journey.
Can the book show kilometres instead?
The route's units follow the tools' settings — generate the route in metric and the book prints metric legs.
Is a roadbook legal to read while driving?
It is a passenger's document. Drivers glance at navigation lawfully; roadbooks are read aloud by co-drivers, as rallying intended.
Can I annotate it?
It is paper's destiny. Print, scribble, survive — the PDF regenerates clean next trip.
